title: EMG Analysis: Preprocessing, Amplitude, and Onset Detection
text: PhysioEMG provides suite functions surface electromyography (EMG) analysis built PhysioExperiment data model. vignette demonstrates core workflow EMG signal processing: creating EMG data objects, extracting amplitude envelopes, normalizing amplitudes, detecting muscle activation onsets.

title: EMG Analysis: Preprocessing, Amplitude, and Onset Detection
text: PhysioEMG includes synthetic data generators testing demonstration. make_emg() function creates multi-channel EMG PhysioExperiment simulated muscle activity bursts. testing onset detection, make_emg_contraction() generates single-channel signal known contraction window:
code: library(PhysioEMG)  # Create a 4-channel EMG recording at 1000 Hz pe <- make_emg(n_time = 2000, n_channels = 4, sr = 1000) pe  # View the channel metadata SummarizedExperiment::colData(pe) pe_contraction <- make_emg_contraction(   n_time = 5000,   sr = 1000,   contraction_start = 0.3,   contraction_end = 0.7 )

title: EMG Analysis: Preprocessing, Amplitude, and Onset Detection
text: emgEnvelope() function extracts amplitude envelope using one three methods: RMS (root mean square): Computes RMS sliding window. Best general-purpose amplitude tracking. Hilbert: Uses analytic signal via Hilbert transform. Provides instantaneous amplitude without windowing artifacts. Lowpass: Rectifies signal applies moving-average lowpass filter. simple computationally efficient approach.
code: # RMS envelope with 50 ms window pe_env <- emgEnvelope(pe, method = "rms", window_ms = 50)  # The envelope is stored as a new assay SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(pe_env) # [1] "raw"      "envelope" # Hilbert envelope for instantaneous amplitude pe_hilbert <- emgEnvelope(pe, method = "hilbert", output_assay = "hilbert_env") # Lowpass envelope with 6 Hz cutoff pe_lp <- emgEnvelope(pe, method = "lowpass", cutoff = 6, output_assay = "lp_env")

title: EMG Analysis: Preprocessing, Amplitude, and Onset Detection
text: EMG amplitudes vary across subjects recording sessions. Normalization enables meaningful comparisons. PhysioEMG supports two normalization methods via emgAmplitudeNormalize(): MVC (maximum voluntary contraction): Divides peak separate MVC trial, yielding percentage--MVC units. Peak: Divides within-trial peak channel ranges 0 1.
code: # Peak normalization (no external reference needed) pe_norm <- emgAmplitudeNormalize(pe_env, method = "peak", assay_name = "envelope")  # Check the normalized values range from 0 to 1 range(SummarizedExperiment::assay(pe_norm, "normalized")) # MVC normalization requires a separate MVC trial, enveloped the same way as the # working data so both carry the assay named in `assay_name` ("envelope"). mvc_trial <- emgEnvelope(make_emg(n_time = 1000, n_channels = 4, sr = 1000)) pe_mvc <- emgAmplitudeNormalize(   pe_env,   method = "mvc",   mvc_data = mvc_trial,   assay_name = "envelope" )

title: EMG Analysis: Preprocessing, Amplitude, and Onset Detection
text: Detecting muscle becomes active fundamental many biomechanics analyses. PhysioEMG implements two onset detection methods:

title: EMG Analysis: Preprocessing, Amplitude, and Onset Detection
text: Hodges-Bui method (1996) thresholds rectified EMG signal multiple baseline standard deviations. widely used due simplicity robustness.
code: pe_contraction <- make_emg_contraction(n_time = 5000, sr = 1000)  # Detect onset using Hodges-Bui method result_hb <- emgOnsetDetect(   pe_contraction,   method = "hodges_bui",   threshold_sd = 3,   baseline_sec = 0.2,   min_duration_ms = 50 )  # View detected onsets result_hb$onsets # Expected: onset near 30% of signal (1.5 seconds at 1000 Hz)

title: EMG Analysis: Preprocessing, Amplitude, and Onset Detection
text: Teager-Kaiser method applies Teager-Kaiser energy operator thresholding. can sensitive sudden onsets TKEO responds amplitude frequency changes.
code: result_tk <- emgOnsetDetect(   pe_contraction,   method = "teager_kaiser",   threshold_sd = 3,   baseline_sec = 0.2 )  result_tk$onsets

title: EMG Analysis: Preprocessing, Amplitude, and Onset Detection
text: methods return onset offset data.frames channel, sample, time information:
code: # Multi-channel onset detection pe_multi <- make_emg(n_time = 5000, n_channels = 4, sr = 1000)  onsets_hb <- emgOnsetDetect(pe_multi, method = "hodges_bui") onsets_tk <- emgOnsetDetect(pe_multi, method = "teager_kaiser")  # Compare onset times across methods merge(   onsets_hb$onsets, onsets_tk$onsets,   by = "channel", suffixes = c("_hb", "_tk") )

title: EMG Fatigue Analysis and Muscle Synergy Decomposition
text: vignette covers two advanced EMG analysis capabilities PhysioEMG: Fatigue analysis: Tracking spectral changes time sustained contractions quantify muscle fatigue. Muscle synergy decomposition: Extracting coordinated muscle activation patterns multi-channel EMG using matrix factorization methods.

title: EMG Fatigue Analysis and Muscle Synergy Decomposition
text: Muscle fatigue sustained contractions causes well-documented shift EMG power spectrum toward lower frequencies. occurs fatigued motor units reduced conduction velocity, compresses spectral content. PhysioEMG provides tools track shift quantify fatigue.

title: EMG Fatigue Analysis and Muscle Synergy Decomposition
text: make_emg_fatigue() generator creates synthetic EMG progressively decreasing median frequency, simulating fatiguing isometric contraction:
code: library(PhysioEMG)  pe_fatigue <- make_emg_fatigue(n_time = 10000, sr = 1000) pe_fatigue # 10 seconds of data at 1000 Hz, single channel

title: EMG Fatigue Analysis and Muscle Synergy Decomposition
text: emgFatigue() function divides signal overlapping windows computes median frequency mean frequency window. declining trend median frequency time indicates fatigue. window_sec parameter controls analysis window length. Longer windows provide stable frequency estimates lower temporal resolution. overlap parameter (0 1) controls much adjacent windows overlap:
code: fatigue_results <- emgFatigue(   pe_fatigue,   window_sec = 1.0,   overlap = 0.5 )  head(fatigue_results) # Columns: channel, window, time_sec, median_freq, mean_freq, rms_amplitude # Higher temporal resolution with shorter windows and more overlap fatigue_fine <- emgFatigue(pe_fatigue, window_sec = 0.5, overlap = 0.75)  # Lower resolution with longer windows fatigue_coarse <- emgFatigue(pe_fatigue, window_sec = 2.0, overlap = 0.5)

title: EMG Fatigue Analysis and Muscle Synergy Decomposition
text: emgFatigueIndex() function provides single summary metric comparing median frequency beginning end recording. fatigue index less 1 indicates frequency decrease (fatigue), value near 1 suggests fatigue. initial_pct final_pct parameters control proportion signal used initial final frequency estimates. Larger values provide stable estimates may blur transient changes.
code: fi <- emgFatigueIndex(pe_fatigue, initial_pct = 0.2, final_pct = 0.2) fi # Columns: channel, fatigue_index, initial_mdf, final_mdf  # fatigue_index < 1 indicates fatigue # initial_mdf > final_mdf confirms spectral compression

title: EMG Fatigue Analysis and Muscle Synergy Decomposition
text: detailed spectral characterization, emgSpectralMoments() computes zeroth (M0, total power), first (M1), second (M2) spectral moments sliding windows: mean frequency derived spectral moments (M1/M0) mathematically equivalent mean frequency reported emgFatigue().
code: moments <- emgSpectralMoments(pe_fatigue, window_sec = 1.0, overlap = 0.5) head(moments) # Columns: channel, window, m0, m1, m2  # Derive mean frequency from moments moments$mean_freq <- moments$m1 / moments$m0

title: EMG Fatigue Analysis and Muscle Synergy Decomposition
text: Muscle synergy analysis decomposes multi-channel EMG small number coordinated activation patterns (synergies). synergy consists weight vector (muscles participate) activation profile (synergy active). approach based motor control hypothesis nervous system simplifies movement activating muscles fixed groups.

title: EMG Fatigue Analysis and Muscle Synergy Decomposition
text: PhysioEMG supports three decomposition methods via muscleSynergy(): NMF (non-negative matrix factorization): Constrains weights activations non-negative, physiologically appropriate rectified EMG. commonly used method synergy extraction. PCA (principal component analysis): Finds orthogonal components explain maximum variance. Fast allows negative values. ICA (independent component analysis): Finds statistically independent components. Useful synergies may overlap temporally.

title: EMG Fatigue Analysis and Muscle Synergy Decomposition
code: # Create multi-channel EMG (8 muscles) pe_multi <- make_emg(n_time = 2000, n_channels = 8, sr = 1000)  # Extract 3 synergies using NMF syn_nmf <- muscleSynergy(   pe_multi,   n_synergies = 3,   method = "nmf",   max_iter = 200,   tol = 1e-4 )  # Examine results str(syn_nmf) # W: 3 x 8 weight matrix (synergies x muscles) # H: 2000 x 3 activation matrix (time x synergies) # vaf: variance accounted for (0-1) # method: "nmf"  cat("Variance accounted for:", round(syn_nmf$vaf, 3), "\n")

text: common approach extract synergies increasing numbers look “elbow” VAF curve, use VAF threshold (e.g., 0.90):
code: vaf_values <- numeric(6) for (n in 1:6) {   result <- muscleSynergy(pe_multi, n_synergies = n, method = "nmf")   vaf_values[n] <- result$vaf }  # Find minimum synergies for 90% VAF n_selected <- which(vaf_values >= 0.90)[1] cat("Selected", n_selected, "synergies (VAF =", round(vaf_values[n_selected], 3), ")\n")

")  # Reconstruct using 3 synergies recon_3 <- synergyReconstruct(syn_full, n_synergies = 3) cat("VAF with 3 synergies:", round(recon_3$vaf, 3), "

what: Detect EMG Muscle Activation Onset and Offset — emgOnsetDetect
title: Detect EMG Muscle Activation Onset and Offset — emgOnsetDetect
text: Identifies muscle activation begins ends. Hodges-Bui method rectifies signal, smooths centered moving average (smooth_ms, original method's low-pass conditioning), thresholds smoothed trace multiple baseline standard deviations. Teager-Kaiser method applies Teager-Kaiser energy operator, rectify--smooth conditioning, thresholding. Without smoothing (smooth_ms = 0) rectified band-limited signal dips threshold every carrier zero-crossing, contiguous suprathreshold runs rarely reach min_duration_ms genuine bursts go undetected. Bonato method uses statistical double-threshold (optionally whitened) signal, declaring activation least r m successive samples exceed chi-square threshold set target false-alarm probability. AGLR method applies Staude & Wolf's approximated generalized-likelihood-ratio change detector variance increase refines onset estimated change point.

title: PhysioEMG 0.2.0
text: Initial release standalone package x-biosignal ecosystem, split PhysioExperiment monorepo. PhysioEMG provides electromyography (EMG) analysis PhysioExperiment objects, spanning amplitude, timing, spectral fatigue, muscle synergy, inter-muscular network methods.

title: PhysioEMG 0.2.0
text: emgEnvelope() extracts amplitude envelope via sliding-window RMS (O(1) prefix-sum implementation), Hilbert analytic signal, rectification moving-average lowpass filter. emgAmplitudeNormalize() normalizes amplitude maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) within-trial peak. emgOnsetDetect() detects activation onsets offsets using Hodges-Bui baseline-SD threshold Teager-Kaiser energy operator, minimum-duration gate reject spurious bursts. emgFatigue() tracks windowed median mean frequency plus RMS amplitude characterize myoelectric fatigue. emgFatigueIndex() summarizes fatigue final--initial median frequency ratio. emgSpectralMoments() computes spectral moments (M0, M1, M2) sliding windows. muscleSynergy() factorizes multi-channel EMG synergies via NMF, PCA, ICA, reporting weight activation matrices variance-accounted-(VAF). synergyReconstruct() rebuilds signals chosen number synergies, synergyCompare() best-match pairs correlates two synergy solutions. Static connectivity via emgCoherenceNetwork() (Welch magnitude-squared coherence), emgPartialCoherenceNetwork() (partial coherence inverse cross-spectral matrix), emgWPLINetwork() (weighted phase-lag index, optional debiased estimator). Directed connectivity via emgDirectedGCNetwork() using pairwise Granger causality (F-statistic delta-R-squared scoring, p-values). Time-varying connectivity via emgDynamicWaveletNetwork() using Morlet wavelet coherence sliding windows cone--influence masking. emgCoordinationStructure() summarizes network topology (module detection, weighted modularity, efficiency, clustering, participation within-module z-scores). emgInterpretNetworkKG() ranks annotates high-weight edges optional node metadata knowledge-graph links. Synthetic data generators examples testing: make_emg(), make_emg_contraction(), make_emg_fatigue().
